Consult Summary:
Adult male with 3-day history of frequent watery diarrhoea, intermittent left-sided abdominal cramping, initial vomiting, and subjective fever—clinical impression of acute gastroenteritis; conservative management and safety-net advice provided.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Loose, watery diarrhoea for 3 days.  
• Frequency: ~6–7 bowel motions/day.  
• Stool characteristics: Watery; denies blood or mucus.  
• Abdominal pain: Intermittent cramp-like pain, left lower abdomen; non-radiating.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Initial vomiting (now resolved).  
  – Subjective fever at symptom onset (felt hot; no documented temperature).  
  – Weakness/shakiness, loss of appetite.  
  – Able to tolerate fluids; taking mainly soups/smoothies.  
• Onset & potential trigger: Ate Chinese takeaway 4 days ago; symptoms began the following day.  
• Impact on daily life: Needs proximity to toilet; continues to work as an accountant but with difficulty.  
• Pertinent negatives: No blood in stool or vomit, no persistent vomiting, no night sweats, no prior bowel problems.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – well controlled with inhaler.

Medications:
• Asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol (advised) – two tablets up to four times daily as needed (patient education; not yet taken).  
• Oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) – dose/route/frequency not documented (advised).
Allergies: Not recorded.

Social History:
• Lives with wife and two children; one child had isolated vomiting.  
• Occupation: Accountant.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Denies alcohol use.  
• No recreational drug use mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (telephone consultation).  
• Abdomen and systemic exam: Not performed/recorded.

Investigations:
• None performed.  
• Stool culture discussed if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Acute self-limited gastroenteritis, most likely viral; bacterial food-borne illness less likely but considered.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Acute viral gastroenteritis – High likelihood: abrupt onset watery diarrhoea, initial vomiting, subjective fever, household exposure, self-limiting pattern.  
2. Acute bacterial food-borne infection – Moderate likelihood: onset after restaurant meal; abdominal cramps; but absence of blood and lack of similar illness in meal companions lessen probability.  
3. Diverticulitis – Low likelihood: left-sided pain and feverish feeling, but large-volume watery stools predominate and patient appears younger; no constant pain.

Issue 1 – Suspected Viral Gastroenteritis  
• Assessment: 3-day watery diarrhoea with self-limited vomiting; likely viral.  
• Plan:  
  – Oral hydration; advise oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
  – Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) up to four times daily for fever/discomfort (dose provided verbally).  
  – Dietary advice: Continue light diet as tolerated.  
  – Rest: Recommend 2–3 days off work.  
  – Infection control: Hand hygiene; avoid food preparation for others until 48 h symptom-free.  
  – Safety-net: Return or seek care if • diarrhoea >3–4 more days, • inability to keep fluids down, • blood in stool, • high fever, or worsening pain.  
  – Follow-up: Telephone or in-person review in 3–4 days if not improving; stool sample and further tests at that time.

Issue 2 – Rule out Bacterial Food-borne Infection  
• Assessment: Possible given takeaway exposure.  
• Plan: If symptoms persist or worsen, send stool culture ± fecal PCR; consider empirical antibiotics only if pathogen identified or severe/invasive features develop.

Issue 3 – Asthma (stable)  
• Assessment: Well controlled; no exacerbation.  
• Plan: Continue current inhaler therapy.

General plan items: None additional.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: Patient age, allergy status, medication details (name/dose) for inhaler, vitals, and physical examination findings.  
• Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal missing information.
